label: copy-phase fed-back digit 3 in early-middle recall positions of long sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input token is the digit 3 (99.6% of activation mass). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and essentially never on any other input token (a little on m and i). Position gates it strongly: activation is concentrated at recall_idx 3-4 (input = original token 2 or 3) in long sequences (L >= 7), with 3 or more outputs still to go. It peaks at t = 11-13 and is strongest at L = 9, recall_idx 3 (3 as the third original token, e.g. 2 2 3 m o k a l z). It is weak or silent when the 3 is copied back near the end of the sequence, in short sequences (L <= 5), or at recall_idx <= 1. The rate also rises with the number of digits in the sequence, but adding that as a condition hurt F1. Dev: P 0.77, R 0.73, F1 0.75, mass recall 0.88. A soft position dependence that the boolean predicate cannot capture limits the fit.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 3, m, i, v, l, h; least: u, g, 1, e) and the token being output (most: m, 3, h, i, l, v; least: s, f, n, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, t=12, L=9 & t=12.
